headline_marked: Microsoft [[ends Oracle AI cloud deal]], forcing dev migration
headline: Microsoft ends Oracle AI cloud deal, forcing dev migration
summary: Microsoft and Oracle have abruptly terminated their partnership for AI cloud services, impacting hybrid cloud deployments and requiring developers to migrate workloads.
details: The unexpected end of the Microsoft-Oracle partnership for AI cloud services has sent ripples through the cloud ecosystem. In less than 48 hours, the integration allowing hybrid AI workloads between Azure and OCI has been removed from marketplace stores, creating urgent concerns for developers and architects.

For those with large language models (LLMs) distributed across both clouds, this means identifying impacts, comparing costs, and migrating everything to Azure. The article provides a step-by-step guide with practical scripts and a ready-to-use CI/CD playbook.

With the partnership dissolved, integration points have been deactivated. Anyone still using OCI for training or inference must migrate artifacts, reconfigure pipelines, and adjust cost policies. A practical tip is to use a 'blue-green deployment' strategy: set up a new Azure environment, validate inference, and then shut down the OCI cluster to minimize downtime.

Consolidating on Azure can lead to a Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) reduction of 15% to 30% compared to OCI, especially for continuous inference workloads, when utilizing Azure Reserved Instances and Savings Plans.
The same pipeline can be replicated in Azure Pipelines using the Docker task and Kubernetes extension. Simply point the service connection to the same Azure Container Registry (ACR).

Developers do not need to rewrite their entire source code. Adjustments are limited to storage endpoints and the inference client. For example, change 'oci://bucket/model.ckpt' to 'https://meuaccount.blob.core.windows.net/checkpoints/model.ckpt'.
Data migration time depends on volume. For 10TB, using Azure Data Factory in 'Copy' mode with 5GB/s throughput, the transfer takes approximately 6 hours. Plan for low-demand windows.
While it's possible to maintain some workloads on OCI by creating a VPN Site-to-Site between Azure Virtual Network and OCI VCN, be mindful of egress costs and additional latency for inference calls.
Microsoft offers support for this migration. Opening an Azure Migration & Modernization ticket can provide compatibility validation scripts and cost estimates.

The Microsoft-Oracle split is more than just news; it's an architectural shift for those operating in hybrid environments. By following the provided scripts and playbook, teams can prepare, adjust pipelines, and leverage Azure consolidation for improved performance, security, and cost savings.

headline_marked: Meta's Muse [[builds apps from chat]] with new Spaces feature
headline: Meta's Muse builds apps from chat with new Spaces feature
summary: Muse, which already has 10 million users, now turns chat prompts into persistent, self-updating applications connected to your other apps.
details: Meta has rapidly iterated on its Muse AI agent, shipping its second major feature in two days: Spaces. Following the addition of voice capabilities on Thursday, Spaces allows users to describe an idea in chat, and Muse will build a persistent workspace for it, such as a tracker or project board.

These generated spaces live in the sidebar and can be moved to the main tab, allowing users to customize their view. For example, a weekly planner can be front and center during the workweek and then swapped for weekend plans on Saturday.

The most significant aspect of Spaces is its ability to connect to other apps. Once linked, the generated space will automatically update in the background with new information, such as concert dates or price changes, without user intervention.

This evolution marks a shift from Muse being a conversational chatbot to an agent that actively builds and maintains applications. The generated output is no longer just a reply but a persistent artifact with its own data pipeline, like a savings tracker that refreshes from a bank app.

Muse Wonder, a specialized version for developers, is also being integrated into the consumer app. Initially announced for developers on October 12, it will now power Muse experiences for subscribers, indicating Meta's strategy to unify its AI offerings.

The competitive landscape is shifting, with the AI 'moat' moving from the underlying model to the connections and data freshness. Meta's extensive distribution across WhatsApp and Instagram provides a significant advantage, and the company is exploring ways to enable sharing of these generated spaces.

Currently, Spaces are single-user, with collaboration being the next anticipated feature. A potential concern is how these persistent applications will handle outdated information, as there's no current mechanism to display sources or last update times.

The lack of an audit trail or clear indication of data sources for these automatically updating spaces could pose a trust issue. Earning user trust will require a system that can be transparent about its data and updates, not just provide correct answers one at a time.
